uncited: - **NeRF Model**: A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) parameterized by weights $\theta$.
It takes a 3D position $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and a viewing direction $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ as input.
- **CLIP Model**: A pre-trained vision-language model (e.g., CLIP-ViT) that maps images and text to a shared embedding space.
It is used as a frozen discriminator/guidance signal.
**Initialization**: Initialize the NeRF radiance field parameters $\theta$ randomly.
No 3D geometry or multi-view images are required.
**Rendering**: For each viewpoint $\mathbf{c}_i$, render a 2D image $I_i$ by ray-marching through the NeRF.
The ray-marching computes the color $C(\mathbf{r})$ and opacity $\alpha(\mathbf{r})$ along rays $\mathbf{r}$ originating from $\mathbf{c}_i$.
**CLIP Scoring**: Pass each rendered image $I_i$ and the input text caption $T$ into the CLIP model.
**Optimization**: Update the NeRF parameters $\theta$ to maximize the aggregate CLIP score across all sampled views.
Gradient descent is used to optimize $\theta$.
**Iteration**: Repeat steps 2-5 until convergence or a fixed number of iterations.

- **Adversarial Generations**: Using a single CLIP model may lead to adversarial artifacts or poor geometric structure.
- **Time Complexity**: High, due to iterative optimization and repeated CLIP inference for multiple views per step.
- **Memory Complexity**: Moderate, storing the NeRF parameters and CLIP model weights.
- **Limitations**: May suffer from adversarial artifacts if not using ensemble guidance; computationally expensive optimization loop.
- **When to use**: When only text prompts are available and 3D data is absent.
- **When not to use**: When high-fidelity geometry is critical without ensemble guidance, or when computational resources are limited.
It is part of the broader trend of using 2D diffusion models and vision-language models for 3D generation.
